subdomain.name: Telemetry Ingestion & Processing
subdomain.capability: Continuous high-throughput ingestion of raw 1Hz sensor telemetry, physical-boundary validation, out-of-order reconciliation, and append-only retention with windowed streaming broadcast (PulseStream Engine).
subdomain.why_distinct: Has its own rules (sensor metric boundaries, 60s reorder window, append-only revisions), its own language (device vs ingress time) and is the differentiating data foundation for endurance analytics.

ubiquitous_language.definition: Individual 1Hz data point of a sensor metric (heart rate, power, cadence, ground contact time, respiration, swim stroke).
Transmission unit received from a device carrying telemetry samples.
Physical physiological/mechanical limit a metric value must respect (e.g. HR 30-240 BPM).
Demand-driven flow control that lets ingestion absorb bursts without blocking.
t_device: epoch timestamp generated by the device; the chronological ordering basis.
t_ingress: arrival time at the engine; never used for ordering.
60-second tolerance within which delayed packets are re-indexed chronologically.
Appended record that corrects or backfills earlier telemetry without altering it.

bounded_contexts.name: Telemetry Intake & Validation
bounded_contexts.responsibility: Accept ingress packets under backpressure and tag each sample against sensor metric boundaries.
invariants: Every sample is validated against its Sensor Metric Boundary before downstream propagation
Invalid samples are flagged VALIDATION_FAILED and never dropped
Ingestion entry point never blocks I/O on thread pools and applies backpressure

bounded_contexts.name: Backfill Reordering
bounded_contexts.responsibility: Re-index delayed samples chronologically within the reorder window and buffer windowed streams.
invariants: Samples delayed up to 60 seconds are ordered by t_device, not t_ingress

bounded_contexts.name: Telemetry Event Ledger
bounded_contexts.responsibility: Retain raw telemetry as an append-only, auditable event history with revisions for corrections and backfills.
invariants: Stored raw records are append-only and never mutated; corrections append new revisions

assumptions.item: Downstream backpressure-aware broadcast is a publishing responsibility of the contexts, not a separate context.
assumptions.impact_on_boundaries: Could justify a separate broadcasting context if subscriber management appears.

assumptions.item: Ownership of the 60s window versus append-only revisions for late backfills is not explicit.
assumptions.impact_on_boundaries: Reordering and Ledger could merge if atomicity is required.

assumptions.item: Whether metric boundaries vary per sport or athlete beyond given examples; no limits given for ground contact time, respiration, stroke.
assumptions.impact_on_boundaries: Could add a configurable rules context.

assumptions.item: Athlete/activity identity and downstream analytics belong to other subdomains of the platform.
